Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

collapse

Replace rows with group nonmissing counts

Stata 

collapse (count) z=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,z=sum(!is.na(x)),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Replace rows with group means

Stata 

collapse (mean) z=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,z=mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Replace rows with group medians

Stata 

collapse (median) z=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,z=stats::median(x,na.rm=TRUE),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Replace rows with group minima

Stata 

collapse (min) z=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data, z = if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else min(x, na.rm = TRUE), .by = g)

Stata reference · R reference

Replace rows with group totals

Stata 

collapse (sum) z=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,z=sum(x,na.rm=TRUE),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Stata reference · R reference

Collapse integer-frequency-weighted values to a mean

Stata 

collapse (mean) x [fw=w]

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data, x = stats::weighted.mean(x, w))

Stata reference · R reference

Collapse integer-frequency-weighted values to a mean

Stata 

collapse (mean) x [fw=w]

R stats 

data <- data.frame(x=stats::weighted.mean(data$x,data$w))

Differs from Stata Frequency-weighted mean only; no inference or weighted-variance formula is implied.

Stata reference · R reference

Use common complete cases for group summaries

Stata 

collapse (mean) x y, cw by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- data[stats::complete.cases(data[c('x','y')]),]; data <- dplyr::summarise(data,dplyr::across(c(x,y),mean),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

contract

Count observed combinations of two categories

Stata 

contract g h, freq(n)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::count(data,g,h,name='n')

Stata reference · R reference

Include unobserved combinations with zero frequency

Stata 

contract g h, freq(n) zero

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::complete(dplyr::count(data, g, h, name = "n"), g, h, fill = list(n = 0L))

Stata reference · R reference

Replace observations with category frequencies

Stata 

contract g, freq(n)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::count(data,g,name='n')

Stata reference · R reference

Create cumulative frequencies and percentages

Stata 

contract g, freq(n) cfreq(cn) cpercent(cp)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::count(data,g,name='n'); data$cn <- cumsum(data$n); data$cp <- 100*data$cn/sum(data$n)

Stata reference · R reference

Create category frequencies and percentages

Stata 

contract g, freq(n) percent(p)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::count(data,g,name='n'); data$p <- 100*data$n/sum(data$n)

Stata reference · R reference

3 more examples and alternatives

Create category counts from integer frequency weights

Stata 

contract g [fw=w], freq(n)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,n=sum(w),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Include unobserved combinations with zero frequency

Stata 

contract g h, freq(n) zero

R base 

data <- as.data.frame(table(data$g,data$h)); names(data) <- c('g','h','n')

Stata reference · R reference

Exclude missing categories before contracting

Stata 

contract g, nomiss

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::count(data[!is.na(data$g)&data$g!='',,drop=FALSE],g,name='_freq')

Differs from Stata Excludes both empty strings and R NA to match Stata's nonmissing string categories.

Stata reference · R reference

summarize

Get detailed empirical percentiles

Stata 

summarize x, detail

R base 

stats::quantile(data$x,c(.01,.05,.1,.25,.5,.75,.9,.95,.99),na.rm=TRUE,type=2)

Differs from Stata Percentile portion of summarize detail, using R type 2; skewness/kurtosis are not returned here.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute mean-only summary components

Stata 

summarize x, meanonly

R tidystata 

tidystata::summ(data, x)

Differs from Stata Also reports the distinct count and standard deviation.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Compute mean-only summary components

Stata 

summarize x, meanonly

R base 

c(n=sum(!is.na(data$x)),mean=mean(data$x,na.rm=TRUE),min=min(data$x,na.rm=TRUE),max=max(data$x,na.rm=TRUE))

Stata reference · R reference

Make each pairwise contingency table

R tidystata 

tidystata::tab2(data, g, h, k)

1 more examples and alternatives

Make each pairwise contingency table

Stata 

tab2 g h k

R base 

pairs <- utils::combn(c('g','h','k'),2,simplify=FALSE); lapply(pairs,function(p) table(data[[p[1]]],data[[p[2]]]))

Stata reference · R reference

tabdisp

Display a complete table of precomputed cell values

Stata 

tabdisp g h, cellvar(value)

R stats 

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(data[c('g','h')])); stats::xtabs(value~g+h,data=data,na.action=stats::na.pass)

Differs from Stata Requires one row for every cell and unique keys; xtabs would otherwise sum duplicates or fill absent cells with zero.

Stata reference · R reference

tabstat

Summarize nonmissing counts and means by category

Stata 

tabstat x, by(g) statistics(n mean)

R dplyr 

data |> dplyr::group_by(g) |> dplyr::summarise(n=sum(!is.na(x)),mean=mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),.groups='drop')

Stata reference · R reference

Return the mean as a descriptive statistic

Stata 

tabstat x, statistics(mean)

R tidystata 

tidystata::tabstat(data, x, .stat = "mean")

Differs from Stata Returns a one-row summary table rather than a bare number; use the base R version when a scalar is needed.

Stata reference · R reference

tabstat x, statistics(min)

R tidystata 

tidystata::tabstat(data, x, .stat = "min")

Differs from Stata Returns a one-row summary table rather than a bare number; use the base R version when a scalar is needed.

Stata reference · R reference

R tidystata 

tidystata::tabstat(data, x, .stat = "n")

Differs from Stata Returns a one-row summary table rather than a bare number; use the base R version when a scalar is needed.

Stata reference · R reference

Return the median as a descriptive statistic

Stata 

tabstat x, statistics(p50)

R base 

with(data,stats::median(x,na.rm=TRUE))

Differs from Stata Unweighted descriptive statistic; no survey or sampling-design correction is applied.

Differs from Stata Unweighted descriptive statistic; no survey or sampling-design correction is applied.

18 more examples and alternatives

Compare count, mean and spread across numeric columns

Stata 

tabstat x y, statistics(n mean sd) columns(statistics)

R tidystata 

tidystata::tabstat(data, x, y, .stat = c("n", "mean", "sd"))

Differs from Stata Rows are variables and columns are statistics, as with columns(statistics).

Stata reference · R reference

Compare count, mean and spread across numeric columns

Stata 

tabstat x y, statistics(n mean sd) columns(statistics)

R base 

sapply(data[c('x','y')],function(z) c(n=sum(!is.na(z)),mean=mean(z,na.rm=TRUE),sd=stats::sd(z,na.rm=TRUE)))

Stata reference · R reference
